plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Parks Fiberlink OLT access device. It reports uptime, CPU utilization, memory (total, free, used, utilization), temperature sensors with alarm status, and interface traffic (enterprise PEN 3893). Fan and power supply status are not collected.
name: Access

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: Average CPU utilization of the Parks OLT (pkCpuSystem scalar, reported in tenths of a percent and divided by 10 at collection).

metrics.name: device_memory_total
metrics.description: Total memory of the Parks OLT (pkMemoryTotal scalar, reported in KB and converted to bytes at collection).

metrics.name: device_memory_free
metrics.description: Free memory of the Parks OLT (pkMemoryFree scalar, reported in KB and converted to bytes at collection).

metrics.name: device_memory_used
metrics.description: Used memory of the Parks OLT (pkMemoryUsed scalar, reported in KB and converted to bytes at collection).

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: Memory utilization of the Parks OLT, computed as pkMemoryUsed / pkMemoryTotal * 100.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: Reading of each temperature sensor of the Parks OLT in degrees Celsius (pkTemperatureSensorValue), labelled by sensor location.

metrics.name: device_temperature_state
metrics.description: Alarm status of each temperature sensor of the Parks OLT (pkTemperatureSensorStatus), normalised so that normal(1) = 1 and limitexceeded(2) = 2.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCInOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCOutOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
